title: Relative Date Input
summary: Stops a date typed the way people say it ("next Fri", "the 10th") from landing on the wrong day by asking when the phrase has two readings.
description: Reads "next Fri", "in 2 weeks", "the 15th" or "23 Oct" against today with date-fns. When a phrase can mean two dates ("next Friday" on a Wednesday, "the 10th" once passed), it shows both and waits for a pick, then offers a rewrite to the explicit date.
catches: Phrases with two honest readings (next/this weekday, next weekend early in the week)
Read-back of the resolved date with its relative distance
One-tap rewrite of the field to an unambiguous date
limits: English phrases only; other languages are not parsed
Uses the today you pass (or the device clock) and its time zone
Covers common everyday phrases, not every natural-language form
a11y: Visible <label> on the input; aria-invalid and status via aria-describedby
Two readings form a roving-tabindex radiogroup operated with arrow keys
Read-back renders in a polite live region
After the rewrite, focus returns to the input
stops: Next Friday lands on the wrong day
